overview: The C-9979 Landing Craft is a separatist landing ship whose design philosophy reflects the industrial and strategic priorities of Clone Wars (32–19 BBY). C-9979 landing ships disgorged droid battalions and MTTs across Naboo, Geonosis, and countless invasion beaches. Production estimates place the class at ~1,500 units, though wartime losses, capture, and black-market duplication make precise fleet registries unreliable.
history:
Engineering teams first finalized the C-9979 Landing Craft blueprints during the political climate of Clone Wars (32–19 BBY). The separatist landing ship was intended to solve specific fleet gaps—whether planetary assault, convoy escort, starfighter superiority, or terror bombardment—and shipwrights iterated hull plates, reactor output, and crew compartments accordingly.

Once deployed, the C-9979 Landing Craft appeared in fleet actions that defined its reputation. C-9979 landing ships disgorged droid battalions and MTTs across Naboo, Geonosis, and countless invasion beaches. Combat logs show crews exploiting the class's strengths while improvising fixes for known weaknesses under fire, a pattern repeated across every major galactic conflict.

As doctrine evolved, rival factions studied captured C-9979 Landing Craft hulls. Refit yards duplicated weapons mounts and sensor suites; some variants never appeared in official manifests. Estimated production of ~1,500 units therefore understates how many similar silhouettes operated under alternate insignia.

Surviving C-9979 Landing Craft vessels now sit in museum orbits, mercenary fleets, and scrap worlds. Historians treat the class as a measure of how galactic wars industrialize violence—each hull a factory product that outlived the politicians who ordered it.
significance:
The C-9979 Landing Craft demonstrates how separatist landing ship design shapes campaign outcomes. Its layout influenced successor programs and remains a case study in naval academies.

With roughly ~1,500 units hulls associated with Clone Wars (32–19 BBY), the class became a visual symbol of its faction's reach—recognizable in holonet footage and feared in convoy manifests.

Engineers still debate whether the C-9979 Landing Craft prioritized firepower over crew survival; that trade-off defines its legacy in both propaganda and honest after-action reports.
